newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Capital Alliance wins JCI control.
newsitem.headline: Capital Alliance wins JCI control.

text.p: Black empowerment group Capital Alliance Holdings Ltd has won the battle for control of JCI Ltd, South Africa's sixth-largest mining house, Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd said on Tuesday.
Anglo and its affiliate De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd said the African Mining Group Consortium, led by Capital Alliance, would pay 54.50 rand a share for 34.9 percent of JCI.
The purchase price is payable on February 28.
JCI shares closed on Tuesday at 49.00 rand.
Anglo said agreenment on the sale had been reached in principle and a definitive agreement would be entered into shortly when a more detailed announcement would be made.
Capital Alliance, a black-controlled financial services group, had been widely viewed as the frontrunner to clinch the stake.
Anglo said last week it was talking to three groups about the sale, including New African Investments Ltd (Nail).
The divestment had become a priority following the conclusion of the recent sale of the 35 percent controlling interest in conglomerate Johnnies Industrial Corp Ltd (Johnnic) to black businesses.
Anglo has long said it wanted to sell JCI to black interests.
Anlaysts believe JCI management also wanted a fast sale because the company has clear ideas on restructuring and the future direction of JCI.
